dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For natural numbers n, b, and q, this is an indexed inductive type of run packages. Its supplied constructor packages positive dimensions, the relation n = q*b, input vectors, three nonnegative real parameters, a computed value, admissibility proofs, perturbation witnesses, and a proposition-valued right-to-left condition.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The theorem is universally quantified only over inhabitants of this package type. Consequently, every field and proof required by its constructor is an implicit hypothesis, and the statement is vacuous for indices for which no package exists.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects field 7 of a run package, a real number denoted computed.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the computed scalar represented by the perturbed sum and compared with the exact dot product in every error bound.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects field 22 of a run package, a proposition denoted rightToLeft.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the antecedent of the conditional sharper beta bound and conditional sharper error bound.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects field 8 of a run package, the real parameter uBar.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It appears in all beta bounds, in the composite error coefficients, and in the special-case equality uBar = uFma.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects field 9 of a run package, the real parameter uFma.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It helps define the effective parameter and appears in the special-case assumptions uOut <= uFma and uBar = uFma.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects field 10 of a run package, the real parameter uOut.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It helps define the effective parameter and appears in the special-case condition uOut <= uFma.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef007
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects field 5 of a run package, a function x : Fin n -> Real.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the first length-n real vector in the exact dot product, perturbed representation, and absolute-product sum.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef008
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects field 6 of a run package, a function y : Fin n -> Real.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the second length-n real vector in the exact dot product, perturbed representation, and absolute-product sum.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef009
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a real u and natural k, it defines gamma_k(u) = (k*u)/(1-k*u), with k cast to a real number.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives every componentwise perturbation bound and is used to construct all forward-error coefficients.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef010
dependency_coverage.meaning: For x,y : Fin n -> Real, it defines A(x,y) = sum over i in Fin n of |x_i|*|y_i|.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: This nonnegative absolute-product sum scales each absolute error bound.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef011
dependency_coverage.meaning: For reals a and u and naturals q and m, it defines gamma_q(a) + gamma_m(u) + gamma_q(a)*gamma_m(u).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With a equal to the effective parameter and u equal to uBar, it is the baseline coefficient for m = n and the right-to-left coefficient for m = q+b-1.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef012
dependency_coverage.meaning: For x,y : Fin n -> Real, it defines their exact finite dot product S = sum over i in Fin n of x_i*y_i.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The absolute forward error is |S-computed|.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef013
dependency_coverage.meaning: It defines an effective real parameter e by e = uOut if uFma < uOut; otherwise e = 0 if uFma <= uBar; otherwise e = uFma.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The alpha bound and the first part of each composite error coefficient use e. Under uOut <= uFma and uBar = uFma, this definition yields e = 0.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef014
dependency_coverage.meaning: This constructor builds a run package from proofs 0<n, 0<b, 0<q, and n=q*b; vectors x and y; reals computed, uBar, uFma, and uOut; nonnegativity of the three parameters; uBar<=uFma; admissibility q*e<1 and n*uBar<1; stored perturbations alpha0 and beta0 satisfying the perturbed-sum identity and baseline componentwise bounds; a proposition rightToLeft; and, conditionally on that proposition, admissibility and a beta0 bound using q+b-1.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It exposes all restrictions hidden in the type of run. In particular, substantial parts of the existential representation and componentwise bounds are already required when constructing a run, although the target existential witnesses are fresh and need not be definitionally identical to the stored ones.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef015
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a real u and natural k, it is the proposition k*u < 1, with k cast to a real.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The run package requires it for (e,q) and (uBar,n), and conditionally for (uBar,q+b-1), ensuring positive denominators in all gamma quantities used under the corresponding conditions.

binders: The natural numbers n, b, and q are implicitly universally quantified.

The variable run is universally quantified over LocalDef001 n b q, an indexed package carrying vectors x,y : Fin n -> Real, a real computed value, real parameters uBar, uFma, and uOut, a proposition rightToLeft, and the constructor data and proofs described below.
The conclusion existentially quantifies alpha,beta : Fin n -> Real. The same alpha and beta must satisfy all conjuncts.
hypotheses: Inhabitance of the run package entails 0<n, 0<b, 0<q, and n=q*b.
Let e be the effective parameter defined below. The package entails q*e<1 and n*uBar<1.
The package already contains some stored perturbations alpha0,beta0 : Fin n -> Real satisfying computed = sum_i x_i*y_i*(1+alpha0_i)*(1+beta0_i), |alpha0_i|<=gamma_q(e), and |beta0_i|<=gamma_n(uBar).
The package contains an arbitrary proposition rightToLeft. If it holds, the package additionally entails (q+b-1)*uBar<1 and |beta0_i|<=gamma_{q+b-1}(uBar) for every i.
conclusions: There exist alpha,beta : Fin n -> Real satisfying all of the following statements simultaneously.
computed = sum over i in Fin n of x_i*y_i*(1+alpha_i)*(1+beta_i).
For every i in Fin n, |alpha_i| <= gamma_q(e).
For every i in Fin n, |beta_i| <= gamma_n(uBar).
If rightToLeft holds, then for every i, |beta_i| <= gamma_r(uBar), and |S-computed| <= C_r*A, where r=(q+b)-1 in Nat.
If uOut<=uFma and uBar=uFma, then alpha_i=0 for every i and |S-computed| <= gamma_n(uBar)*A.
mathematical_definitions: The index set Fin n consists of i=0,...,n-1.
e = uOut if uFma<uOut; e = 0 if uFma is not less than uOut and uFma<=uBar; otherwise e = uFma.
For a natural k and real u, gamma_k(u) = (k*u)/(1-k*u), with k interpreted as a real number.
S = sum over i in Fin n of x_i*y_i.
A = sum over i in Fin n of |x_i|*|y_i|.
For a natural m, C_m = gamma_q(e) + gamma_m(uBar) + gamma_q(e)*gamma_m(uBar).
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every packaged run with positive natural parameters n,b,q satisfying n=q*b and with the packaged vectors, scalar parameters, admissibility conditions, and preliminary perturbation representation, there are length-n real perturbation vectors alpha and beta such that the computed scalar is exactly the dot-product sum with each term multiplied by (1+alpha_i)(1+beta_i). Every alpha_i is bounded in magnitude by gamma_q(e), and every beta_i is bounded by gamma_n(uBar). The absolute difference between the exact dot product and the computed scalar is at most [gamma_q(e)+gamma_n(uBar)+gamma_q(e)gamma_n(uBar)] times sum_i |x_i||y_i|. If the package's proposition rightToLeft holds, beta and the error satisfy the corresponding sharper bounds with n replaced by q+b-1. Finally, if uOut<=uFma and uBar=uFma, every alpha_i is zero and the error is bounded by gamma_n(uBar) times sum_i |x_i||y_i|.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The theorem does not range over arbitrary n,b,q and arbitrary data independently. It ranges over inhabitants of a package whose constructor already requires n,b,q>0, n=q*b, parameter restrictions, admissibility, and an existing perturbation representation.
For indices or data admitting no LocalDef001 package, the universal statement has no run to which it applies and is therefore vacuous.

The constructor already assumes stored perturbations satisfying the exact perturbed identity and the baseline alpha and beta bounds. Thus those parts of the target do not establish such a representation from unstructured input data.
The existential alpha and beta are not asserted to be unique and are not asserted to equal the perturbations stored in run.
The proposition rightToLeft is an arbitrary Prop field with no encoded mathematical characterization. Both right-to-left refinements are vacuous when that proposition does not hold.
The final refinement is an implication and is vacuous unless both uOut<=uFma and uBar=uFma hold.
Natural subtraction is truncated at zero. Here q>0 and b>0 imply q+b>=2, so (q+b)-1 agrees with ordinary subtraction and is positive.

Lean's real division is total, but the package's strict inequalities q*e<1, n*uBar<1, and conditionally r*uBar<1 ensure that every gamma denominator used in an asserted bound is positive under the relevant condition.
The vectors x and y otherwise have arbitrary real entries. No nonzero assumption, normalization, sign condition, or bound on their components is encoded.
The error guarantee is absolute and scaled by A=sum_i |x_i||y_i|. No relative-error bound, normwise relative guarantee, or lower bound on the exact dot product is asserted.
No operational or algorithmic meaning of computed, uBar, uFma, uOut, or rightToLeft is encoded beyond the displayed fields, equations, inequalities, and package constraints.
